en: Jinling
Jiankang
Baixia
Jiangning

modern_status.zh: 今秦淮区夫子庙景区内的步行街，仍名乌衣巷。
modern_status.en: A pedestrian street still named Wuyi Lane, inside the Confucius Temple (Qinhuai) scenic area.

modern_status.zh: 原桥已不存，旧址在今镇淮桥一带。
modern_status.en: Original bridge lost; site lay near today's Zhenhuai Bridge over the Qinhuai.

modern_status.zh: 故址在今南京城西南隅凤凰山，台已不存。
modern_status.en: Former site on Phoenix Hill in the city's southwest; the terrace no longer survives.

modern_status.zh: 石头城遗址公园，仍存部分城垣（“鬼脸城”）。
modern_status.en: Stone City Ruins Park; a stretch of the old rampart (the 'Ghost Face Wall') still stands.

modern_status.zh: 具体酒肆无考，泛指金陵城内秦淮一带。
modern_status.en: No specific tavern identified; broadly the Qinhuai district of old Jinling.

modern_status.zh: 古为长江沙洲，今已与陆地相连，江东门外一带。
modern_status.en: Once a sandbar in the Yangtze, now joined to land near Jiangdongmen.

modern_status.zh: 六朝宫城遗迹，今玄武湖南侧、鸡鸣寺一带。
modern_status.en: Six Dynasties palace-city ruins, near Jiming Temple south of Xuanwu Lake.

en: Beside the Zhuque Bridge, wildflowers bloom in the grass;
at the mouth of Black-robe Lane the setting sun hangs low.
The swallows that once nested in the halls of the Wang and Xie clans
now fly into the homes of ordinary folk.
(prose paraphrase, original translation, license: CC0)

note.zh: 刘禹锡作《金陵五题》时自序未曾亲至金陵，乃凭想象与传闻而作——这正是“描写于此”而非“作于此”的典型。
note.en: By his own preface to the Five Themes of Jinling, Liu Yuxi had never visited Jinling — written from imagination. The classic case of 'describes here', not 'written here'.

en: impermanence
fallen glory
ubi sunt

note.zh: 开元十四年春离金陵赴扬州时作。
note.en: Written ~726 as Li Bai left Jinling for Yangzhou.

en: Wind blows willow-down, the whole shop sweet with its scent;
a Wu girl presses the wine and calls the guests to taste.
The young men of Jinling have come to see me off —
about to go, not going, each drains his cup.
Go, ask the east-flowing water:
between it and a parting's grief, which runs longer?
(prose paraphrase, original translation, license: CC0)

note.zh: 作于金陵，但具体酒肆位置无考，故地点可信度为中。
note.en: Composed in Jinling, but the exact tavern is unknown — hence location confidence is medium.

en: farewell
friendship

note.zh: 创作背景说法不一：一说天宝年间被排挤离长安南游金陵所作，一说流放夜郎遇赦后作。
note.en: Date disputed: possibly ~747 after being forced from Chang'an, or after his later pardon. Sources disagree.

en: On Phoenix Terrace the phoenixes once roamed;
the birds are gone, the terrace bare, the river flows on alone.
The flowers of the Wu palace are buried in shadowed paths,
the lords of the Jin age are now ancient mounds.
The Three Peaks fall half beyond the blue sky;
the river splits in two around Egret Isle.
It is always the drifting clouds that can hide the sun —
Chang'an out of sight, and the heart fills with grief.
(prose paraphrase, original translation, license: CC0)

note.zh: 传李白登凤凰台所作，意在与崔颢《黄鹤楼》争胜；台址已不存，且创作年代有争议。
note.en: Traditionally written atop the terrace as a deliberate rival to Cui Hao's Yellow Crane Tower. The terrace is lost and the date is contested.

en: meditation on the past
political grief
Hills ring the old kingdom, still circling it round;
the tide beats the empty city and draws back, forlorn.
East of the Qinhuai the moon of former days
still climbs, deep in the night, past the battlements.
(prose paraphrase, original translation, license: CC0)

note.zh: 同属《金陵五题》，凭想象而作；但石头城遗址今仍可访，地点可信度高。
note.en: Also from the Five Themes (written from imagination), but the Stone City ruins survive and are visitable — location confidence high.

en: meditation on the past
rise and fall of dynasties
Who said sorrow cannot be painted?
The painter's heart follows the feeling of the age.
Look at these six scenes of the Southern Dynasties:
old trees and cold clouds fill the fallen city.
(prose paraphrase, original translation, license: CC0)

note.zh: 题画诗，咏南朝金陵之衰，非实地所作，泛指六朝故城（台城一带）。
note.en: A poem on a painting, lamenting the fallen Southern capital — not written on-site; points broadly to the Six Dynasties palace area.

en: meditation on the past
Six Dynasties
poem on a painting
River rain drifts thin, the river grass grows even;
the Six Dynasties pass like a dream, birds cry to no one.
Most heartless of all is the willow of Taicheng —
still, as ever, it veils ten li of dyke in mist.
(prose paraphrase, original translation, license: CC0)

note.zh: 凭吊台城旧址而作，地点明确。
note.en: An elegy at the Taicheng site; location is clearly identified.

en: meditation on the past
dream of vanished dynasties
